Daily Brief

The day's headlines are dominated by shifting dynamics in both US-Iran tensions and European migration policy. President Trump announced that negotiations with Iran will resume Monday after calling off planned strikes, citing requests from Gulf allies including Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman [BBC], [Globe and Mail], [Financial Times]. Oil prices fell on the news, though Iran's foreign ministry denied plans to receive a US delegation directly. In Europe, the EU has called an emergency meeting of interior ministers for Tuesday following the mass crossing of some 60,000 migrants into Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco, which left at least 72 dead [BBC], [Guardian], [RFI]. The crisis has sparked sharp divisions, with Italy suspending Schengen arrangements with Spain—a move condemned by Madrid as 'selfish and unlawful.' Meanwhile, Japan and the United States confirmed their first joint currency intervention since 2011, spending tens of billions to halt the yen's slide to 40-year lows [BBC], [Nikkei Asia], [Financial Times]. In the Russia-Ukraine war, Kyiv intensified deep strikes on Russian territory, hitting oil refineries and Wildberries warehouses, while Moscow reported eight deaths from overnight drone attacks [BBC], [France 24], [Globe and Mail]. Cuba suffered another nationwide blackout as its fragile grid collapsed again [Al Jazeera], [Le Monde].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Trump Calls Off Iran Strikes, Says Negotiations to Resume Monday

  • President Trump announced new talks with Iran will begin Monday afternoon after canceling what he described as planned 'massive' strikes at the request of Gulf allies including Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar.
  • Trump stated that the 'parameters' of a deal covering the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program had been reached, though Iran's foreign ministry denied plans to receive a US delegation or send officials to Washington.
  • Global oil prices fell on the news; Trump declined to set a deadline for reaching a final agreement, saying 'We're ready to go anytime we want.'
  • Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly urged Trump to pursue diplomacy over military action during a Saturday phone call.

02 Policy

EU Calls Emergency Meeting as Ceuta Migrant Crisis Sparks Bloc Divisions

  • The EU will hold an emergency meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday after approximately 60,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta enclave, with at least 72 confirmed dead.
  • Italy suspended its Schengen free-movement arrangement with Spain, a move backed by Finland and Denmark; Spain condemned the response as 'selfish, polarising and unlawful.'
  • Twenty-two EU member states issued a joint letter calling for coordinated action and strengthened external borders, citing concerns about 'hybrid threats' creating perceptions that illegal entry is possible.
  • Spanish officials report nearly all migrants have returned to Morocco; police began installing a 500-metre floating barrier off the border.

03 Economics

US and Japan Conduct First Joint Currency Intervention Since 2011 to Halt Yen Slide

  • Japan and the United States jointly intervened in currency markets Friday after the yen fell to a 40-year low against the dollar, the first coordinated action since the 2011 earthquake and tsunami.
  • Bank of Japan data indicated Tokyo may have sold nearly $59 billion in US dollars to buy yen; a Reuters photograph showed Treasury Secretary Bessent's notes referencing a $5-10 billion US purchase.
  • Both countries' finance officials stated they will not hesitate to conduct further joint interventions if necessary.
  • The yen strengthened to the 155 range against the dollar Monday morning as markets remain wary of additional intervention.

04 Conflict

Ukraine Intensifies Deep Strikes on Russian Oil Infrastructure and Warehouses

  • Ukraine struck a major oil refinery and the Engels strategic aviation airfield in Russia's Saratov region, some 600km from Ukraine's border, along with targets in Kaluga and Bryansk regions.
  • Russia reported eight people killed in overnight Ukrainian drone strikes, with 635 drones shot down or intercepted; a child was among the dead in Belgorod region.
  • Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, reported another warehouse fire after a drone attack in Vladimir region—approximately the twentieth strike on the company's facilities since mid-July.
  • A suspected bomb attack at a Moscow restaurant killed three and injured 21; the Russian Embassy blamed Ukraine, with unconfirmed reports suggesting a senior military commander may have been the target.

05 Society

Cuba's National Power Grid Collapses in Latest Nationwide Blackout

  • Cuba's national electricity grid collapsed late Sunday, plunging the island into a widespread blackout—the latest in a series of total grid failures this year.
  • The state-run Electric Union announced the collapse but did not identify its cause, the extent of disruption, or when power would be restored.
  • Prior to the nationwide failure, Havana's electricity company had reported outages from damaged transformers, circuit failures, and planned cuts due to insufficient generating capacity.
  • Cuba's electricity system has deteriorated significantly amid persistent shortages of fuel and replacement parts.
